## 一句话判断

代理评测的范式应当从「模型说了什么」转向「系统留下了什么」：这份微软 × Hugging Face 的联合研究用 507 个有状态业务流程、每任务重复 20 次，把代理的可靠性与成本第一次放到了可执行的数据库终态上。

## 1. 方法：轨迹是声明，数据库状态才是证据

每个任务给定初始后端状态、用户目标、MCP 工具集与领域策略，由确定性检查核对最终状态（477/507 纯状态判定，30 个附带答复评分）；同一任务的两次尝试永远不共享数据库行。评分不看工具调用是否工整、不看模型的自述。总计 121,680 次有效试验、12 个模型、507 × 20 次重复。开篇例子很典型：客服代理九次工具调用全部合法，却把工单标成 resolved，而承运商异常未解、要求的终态应为 on hold——「一个只查工具调用的评分器会看到九个漂亮的调用；数据库不同意。」

## 2. 最扎心的发现：67% 的失败是「静默失败」

79,853 次失败里有 67.24% 终止得干干净净：没用错工具、没报工具错误、模型自信收尾。可执行检查却发现字段值错误 77.61%、多余副作用 43.30%、漏做必备动作 25.36%（有重叠）。也就是说，只看轨迹或只看有没有报错的验收方式，会漏掉三分之二的问题。

## 3. 能力 ≠ 可靠性：pass@20 与「20/20」是两回事

Kimi-K3 是全场覆盖面最广的模型（93.89% 的任务至少解出一次，477/507），但在全部 20 次都通过的任务上只有 13.41%（68/507）；Claude Opus 5 一次解出的任务更少（79.09%），却把 47.53% 的任务做到 20/20 全过。更刺痛的是：Opus 5.5 每个维度比 Opus 5 涨了半分（67.16% vs 66.50%），而 20/20 的任务数一模一样（241）——半分头名精度没有换来任何可靠性。单次成功只说明模型能做，重复 20 次才回答它是否总会做对。

## 4. 可靠性的价格

成本要分两档看：每次成功尝试的成本（GPT-5.6 Sol 最低 $0.127）与每个「可靠任务」的成本（20 次全过）。后者前排：GPT-5.4 $6.80（128 个可靠任务）、GPT-6 Astra $7.45（231）、Claude Opus 5.5 $7.80（241）。「拿到正确答案最便宜的方式，不是拿到可靠答案最便宜的方式。」单次能力能保住多少：只有 Astra 保留 78%、Opus 5.5/5 保留 71%，而 GLM-5.1、Kimi-K2.6、DeepSeek-V4-Pro 只剩约 8%。

约八成失败是工具处理问题：79.9% 工具使用、10.3% 状态更新错误、7.0% 未完成用户诉求、2.9% 没有状态变更。多数代理是「走得够远、但翻不过工具错误与空查询」——这是重试与错误恢复问题，其次才是模型问题。作者建议：提交前检查终态而不是相信模型的总结；给工具面做减法；不可廉价回滚的变更强制人工批准。评测环境（数据集 + 评测器）已在 Hugging Face / OpenEnv 开源，可以拿自己的模型复现单任务。

如果你在给公司搭代理或验收别人的代理系统，这是今晚最该读的一篇：它把「代理到底可不可信」拆成可复现的度量（终态、20 次重复、每个可靠任务的成本），并附送一整套能直接跑的评测环境。和下面 Unit 42 那篇一起读，是「如何验证」与「如何被攻破」的完整一课。

## 一句话判断

一篇把「托管代理运行时最窄的那个缺口」演示到字节级的安全研究：默认配置下 shell 工具以 root 跑在与解析凭据相同的进程空间里，一条间接注入就能把身份保险库里的 JWT 掏出来——而 AWS 把报告关成了 informative，把缓解责任留给了使用者。

## 1. 背景：保险库保护静态与传输，不保护「使用中」

AgentCore Identity 把凭据加密存储（KMS + IAM 管控），引用时用 ARN；但运行时要把 ARN 解析成明文才能拿去调下游服务——解析结果就躺在 harness 进程（PID 1，python3.10 -m loopy.server）的堆里。而 harness 默认自带 shell 与 file_operations 两个内置工具，与 PID 1 同 UID，shell 直接以 root 运行——「不需要任何配置错误，这就是开箱状态」。

## 2. 攻击链：从工单里的一行注入到全网可重放的 JWT

研究者先直接提示模型执行侦察命令，被拒两次；于是换上更顺从的模型 + 间接提示注入，把载荷藏进支持工单的 HTML 注释，指令只有一行「curl 我们的脚本 | python3」——不需要精确语法，一次到位。随后在环境内 whoami/id 发现 root，读 /proc/1/maps 拿到内存布局、再扫 /proc/1/mem 的堆，从进程内存里揪出 1,034 字节的 JWT 与 MCP 服务器 URL，一并 POST 到攻击者 webhook，再从自己的笔记本（无任何 AWS 凭据）重放：列出 MCP 工具、调用 lookup_customer 拿到客户 PII、创建工单。

## 3. 被偷的是谁的凭据：操作者的服务账号，不是终端用户的

这是全文最值得记住的边界：调用者只有 bedrock-agentcore:InvokeHarness 权限；harness 的执行角色却能触达操作者接入的每一个下游服务。保险库里那份跨所有用户会话复用的 mcp-service 凭据，才是落进堆、被带走的那一份——终端用户自己的会话 JWT 反而干不了这事（短命、不可预注册）。用户从未拥有、也本不该拥有的权限，被一次注入拿走了。

## 4. AWS 的立场与 allowedTools 的坑

AWS 以共享责任模型关闭报告（informative），把 allowedTools 收窄与出站过滤列为客户侧控制。研究者提醒一个细节：allowedTools 在 InvokeHarness 时生效而不是 CreateHarness——参数灵活，但不知道就会漏；内置 shell 与 file_operations 对每个会话默认开启，不需要你显式同意。

## 5. 给运维者的三条与给平台作者的一条

运维三条：按会话把 allowedTools 收到最小（不需要的会话就不给 shell）；把保险库服务账号按最小权限绑定下游集成（泄露的凭据只值它作用域内的东西）；盯紧 harness 容器的出站流量——出现清单外的端点就是「注入正在发生」的证据，而不是配置漂移。给平台作者一条：把 harness 给模型的每个能力当成攻击面原语；任何运行时解析的凭据，要么放在 shell 读不到的地方，要么把 shell 与凭据解析进程隔离——「保险库只防静态与传输，使用中的明文是另一个问题。」

## 我的推荐

如果你在自己的基础设施上跑带 shell 的代理，或正在评估任意托管代理运行时，这篇是今晚的必修课：它把「提示注入能造成什么」从抽象恐惧变成一条从工单注释到客户 PII 的完整、可重放的攻击链，还给出三条可以直接进 checklist 的加固项。

key_points: 捕获点在 ProxySQL：客户端无关、无应用改动；Log Processor 按集群分区、按原始顺序重组事务、5 分钟分桶，并重写 INSERT 固定 last_insert_id。
调度器用同一「预期开始时间」让同批 worker 同时开跑，复现原始并发节奏；Replay only 做压测、Replay and compare 做升级比对。
战果：某查询 0.03s→2.6s（每 join 读 273MB）、自增 ID 交错、无排序键 + LIMIT 的静默漂移都被提前拦下；写 +80% 时提交延迟 6ms→34ms。
合规姿态：日志仅测试窗口开启、全程加密、回放只在生产等价环境——这些约束是这套系统能存在的前提。

## 一句话判断

Airbnb 把「用真实生产流量给数据库做测试」工程化到底的一篇：在 ProxySQL 上建无侵入的捕获点，把事务重建成可回放数据集，用几千个 worker 按原始节奏重放——5.7→8.0 升级零重大事故，容量规划先在离线环境里把天花板撞出来。

## 1. 动机：合成基准测的是你想象的负载

sysbench 之类的合成负载盖不住生产的查询光谱；performance_schema 的 digest 只是摘要，无法复现问题。他们要三个能力：真实流量压测（按 1x/2x/3x 或目标 QPS 回放，为峰值季节做容量规划）、升级与迁移的兼容性验证（同一流量打到两个目标比对结果）、以及把事故工作负载离线重放来定位与验证修复。

## 2. 架构：三个组件，一个无侵入捕获点

捕获点在 ProxySQL——理解 MySQL 协议、本来就站在应用与数据库之间，客户端无关、无需应用改动。Log Mover 边车把查询日志送进对象存储；Log Processor 离线把多集群混在一起的二进制日志按集群分区、按原始顺序重组每个事务、以 5 分钟窗口分桶，并做一件不起眼但关键的事：把 INSERT 重写为显式携带 last_insert_id（不同引擎/版本的自增分配方式不同，否则后续依赖自增 ID 的读会漂移、制造假阳性）。代价是不再顺带测试目标库的原生自增，作者明确接受这个取舍。

## 3. 回放器：把「同一起跑线」做成了工程

API Server + 任务调度器 + 可横向扩展至数千实例的 worker。调度器按日志文件切任务、给同批任务同一个「预期开始时间」，worker 各自等待该信号后同时开跑——这样复现的是原始并发与节奏，而不是各自孤立地回放五分钟文件。两种模式：Replay only（负载测试，追踪错误、分位延迟、资源利用率）与 Replay and compare（同一查询打两个库、diff 结果，用于升级验证）。

## 4. 战果：把「回归」在离线阶段撞出来

5.7→8.0 升级中抓到的实例：某查询模式延迟从 0.03s 飙到 2.6s（每 join 读 273MB 而非 5MB，定位到 8.0.20+ 排序时读行的变化）；先对 5.7 带/不带 query cache 回放做二分、再与 8.0 对比，暴露出应用重复发送可缓存查询的问题。可靠性上也拦下两类经典坑：innodb_autoinc_lock_mode 默认变更带来的交错自增 ID；没有 ORDER BY 或排序键不唯一 + LIMIT 的查询在新引擎上悄悄返回不同行——提前和业务团队补上显式排序。容量侧：某大集群写流量 +80% 时平均提交延迟从约 6ms 涨到 34ms，远在真实流量撞墙前标出天花板。

## 5. 合规姿态与边界

查询日志只对测试集群、测试窗口开启；传输与静态全程加密；访问限数据库基础设施团队；回放只在生产等价环境里跑，绝不落到低阶环境、也不复制到开发层。这套约束不是装饰——它是这套系统能存在的前提，也提醒读者：回放生产流量的能力必须配套同等强度的治理。

## 我的推荐

给所有「改了数据库心里没底」的团队：这篇把捕捉、重建、回放、比对每一步的取舍都摊开了，包括 last_insert_id 重写、同起跑线调度这些魔鬼细节，并用 5.7→8.0 的实战成绩证明值得建。哪怕你不做数据库，这套「用真实负载给变更上保险」的方法论也适用于任何关键基础设施的升级决策。

items.title: NTS: Authenticated Time at Meta (12 minute read)

items.score_reason: 五种 PostgreSQL 连接池的横向评测
items.highlight: PostgreSQL 连接池横评：对比 Pgpool-II、PgBouncer、RDS Proxy、PgCat、PgDog 的进程模型、事务池化下会话状态处理与坑点；只做池化选 PgBouncer，读写分离或分片用 PgDog。
items.excerpt: PostgreSQL’s connection model is the one it has always had: one client connection, one operating system process. Each backend is a `fork()` of the postmaster, with its own catalog caches, its own memory contexts, and its own opinions about `work_mem`. This is simple and it is expensive. Connection setup costs a fork, an authentication exchange and (these days) a TLS handshake. Every connection that exists costs memory whether it is doing anything or not. And every connection that *is* doing something wants a CPU core, of which the database server has far fewer than the application tier has threads.

items.score_reason: 播客：与 Sam Newman 谈微服务、韧性系统与 AI 的影响
items.highlight: The Pragmatic Engineer 访谈 Sam Newman：微服务堪称架构『最后手段』，分布式系统三条规则（信息传输耗时、资源会下线、资源有限），并警告 AI 时代的认知投降。
items.excerpt: Sam Newman wrote one of the most-read books about microservices (“[Building Microservices](https://samnewman.io/books/building_microservices/)”), but he calls them an architecture of “last resort.”

items.title: Decisions (8 minute read)
items.summary: OpenAI's Decisions API turns text and images into decisions that applications can use. It evaluates text, images, or both and returns typed answers 10 times faster than the Responses API. The Decisions API returns a probability that a condition is true, a choice from a fixed set, or a score against a rubric. These answers can be used to classify content, route requests, and prioritize work in an application.
items.score_reason: OpenAI Decisions API 开发文档：快速决策接口说明
items.highlight: OpenAI 发布 Decisions API 公测：用 predicate、choice、score 三类问题评估文本与图像，输出概率、选项或评分，比 Responses API 快 10 倍，仅支持 gpt-6-luna。
items.excerpt: The Decisions API evaluates text, images, or both and returns typed answers about 10x faster than the Responses API. Get the probability that a condition is true, a choice from a fixed set, or a score against a rubric. Use those answers to classify content, route requests, and prioritize work in your application.

items.title: How to keep learning in the age of LLMs (9 minute read)
items.summary: We used to learn things by doing something wrong first and then taking a lesson out of it. LLMs make everything so fast that we don't want to spend time doing the wrong things, even though it's more beneficial in the long run. The struggle is how the brain actually learns new things. Use AI to help you think through problems rather than just giving you the answer.
items.score_reason: 随笔：LLM 时代如何保持学习节奏
items.highlight: 作者分享在 LLM 时代保持编程学习的方法：让模型以苏格拉底式提问引导自己找答案，把测试与工具等杂活交给它，用分阶段 PLAN 与 REPL 等可视化进度维持动力，并以小步坚持对抗拖延。
items.excerpt: I want to talk about how I keep learning new things in the age of LLMs, because it got really hard. LLMs, AI, agents, whatever you want to call them, can one-shot stuff and kill the entire joy of getting something wrong. I’m mostly talking about programming here, but I think it applies to anything. We used to learn new things like frameworks, programming languages, and patterns by doing something wrong first and then taking a lesson out of it. But now everything is so fast that we don’t want to spend time doing the wrong things, even though it’s more beneficial for us in the long run. That struggle is how your brain actually learns new things.

items.title: Shipping JPEG XL in Chrome (3 minute read)
items.summary: JPEG XL offers 30% to 50% better compression than JPEG, lossless compression, built-in HDR support, lossless JPEG transcoding, and more.
items.score_reason: Chrome 接入 JPEG XL 的技术与性能细节
items.highlight: Chrome 155 起正式支持 JPEG XL 解码：该格式比 JPEG 压缩率高 30–50%，支持无损压缩、HDR 与 JPEG 无损转码；解码器用纯 Rust 重写以消除内存安全漏洞，并用 SIMD 优化性能。
items.excerpt: We're excited to announce that Chrome is shipping decoding support for the JPEG XL (.jxl) image format starting from Chrome 155. JPEG XL is a next-generation image format designed to meet the needs of modern web developers and photographers. It offers 30-50% better compression than JPEG, lossless compression, built-in HDR support, lossless JPEG transcoding, and more.

items.title: EmbeddingGemma 2 (5 minute read)
items.summary: EmbeddingGemma 2 is a 740M-parameter model that maps text, code, images, audio, and video into a shared embedding space. Built for on-device inference and released under Apache 2.0, it enables multimodal search and retrieval without sending data to the cloud.
items.score_reason: EmbeddingGemma 2：端侧多模态嵌入模型发布
items.highlight: 谷歌发布开源多模态嵌入模型EmbeddingGemma 2：740M参数、Apache 2.0许可，将文本、代码、图像、视频和音频统一到同一嵌入空间，并支持向量维度截断，可在端侧高效运行。
items.excerpt: We introduced EmbeddingGemma last year to provide a lightweight option for high-quality text embeddings, to help your apps organize, search, and connect information directly on consumer hardware. The developer community’s response blew past our expectations. With more than 20 million downloads, builders have used it to power smarter on-device search tools and privacy-first retrieval augmented generation (RAG) pipelines.

items.title: Introducing Personal Agent Protocol (5 minute read)
items.summary: The Personal Agent Protocol is an open standard that Meta and Sierra are developing along with other industry partners. It is designed to handle authentication, empower consumers, and give companies visibility into what personal agents do through their websites, APIs, or company agents. Consumers decide what access to give their personal agents, and companies set parameters for what those agents can do. The protocol is open for anyone to implement.
items.score_reason: Meta 与 Sierra 推动 Personal Agent Protocol 开放标准
items.highlight: Sierra与Meta联合Shopify、Stripe等推出个人代理协议PAP，定义个人AI代理与企业交互的开放标准：基于OAuth，用户自控权限，代理可通过网站、API或企业代理完成任务。
items.excerpt: Personal AI agents are taking the world by storm. People are using them to do everything from scheduling appointments to booking flights and shopping for car insurance. It’s extraordinary how fast AI is changing consumer behavior and how many of us are having those incredible “wait, it just did that” moments with our personal agents. Unsurprisingly companies are asking how they can best respect their consumers’ choices while also protecting their privacy and security.

items.highlight: NVIDIA 发布 AICR v1.0，以版本锁定、带签名验证证据的配方管理 GPU Kubernetes 集群配置，涵盖快照、配方、部署产物与验证，支持 Helm、Argo CD、Flux 等工具并承诺 v1.x 接口兼容。
items.excerpt: GPU-accelerated Kubernetes clusters depend on compatible versions across dozens of components, each on its own release cycle: host kernels, GPU drivers, container runtimes, networking, storage, operators, and workload frameworks.

items.title: How to Read Code (8 minute read)
items.summary: Code is easier to understand through several focused passes than through a linear read from top to bottom. Trace one execution path or piece of data at a time, inspect call sites outside the diff, and save the final line-by-line review after the broader structure is clear.
items.score_reason: 方法论：多轮聚焦式阅读代码
items.highlight: Sean Goedecke 主张读代码要像读数学论文一样做多轮「二分扫描」：先把握整体调用结构、再沿线索跳读细节，最后才从头细读；他同时强调 AI 生成的代码仍必须由人仔细阅读，因为模型的技术价值观未必与你一致。
items.excerpt: Everyone knows how to read a book. Beginning at the first page, you read each word in order, stopping periodically to think, until you arrive at the last word on the last page. That’s how you read a newspaper article, or a poem, or an email. Why would reading code be any different?

items.title: The Grand Unifying Architecture of Frontend (13 minute read)
items.summary: Frontend architectures can be understood as three layers: navigation, server-owned content, and client-owned affordances such as optimistic state. The framework maps HTMX, LiveView, Astro, React Server Components, SPAs, and sync engines onto the same model, with differences in transport, lifetime, and how much code reaches the client.
items.score_reason: 前端架构的统一框架：导航、服务端内容与客户端能力
items.highlight: Ryan Carniato 提出前端统一架构由三层责任组成：导航与交互在客户端、内容在服务器；他以 Solid 2.0 的 use server 动作、线上响应式图与乐观更新展示同一套原语可覆盖从 HTMX 到 SPA 的光谱。
items.excerpt: I used to joke that the history of frontend development could be retraced by following the argument of who owned the state. And the truth is both sides have gone back and forth on this over the years. We started on the document web where state was on the server. Then we added JavaScript and Applets where we could have stateful things in the client. But developers at the time didn't like either much and tried to wire state across both sides in their server languages and we got ASP.NET and the like.

items.title: WordPress libheif RCE: Exploit Chain (11 minute read)
items.summary: Fortbridge has published the first public exploit chain for a libheif heap overflow (GHSA-x8r2-mggj-j6wr) originally discovered by Alex Thomas and Wordfence. By uploading crafted HEIC images via the WordPress Media Library, an authenticated attacker can defeat ASLR using pixel values in generated JPEGs and hijack a C++ virtual table pointer to achieve remote code execution. Administrators should update libheif to 1.23.3, disable unused HEIC/AVIF uploads, and treat repeated PHP-FPM 503 errors on image uploads as security events.
items.score_reason: WordPress libheif 堆溢出漏洞利用链公开
items.highlight: 披露WordPress libheif堆溢出RCE完整利用链：认证作者上传特制HEIC，从衍生图返回像素恢复地址并识别精确构建绕过ASLR，触发溢出劫持C++虚调用执行命令，Ubuntu与Debian实测成功率75%与91.7%。
items.excerpt: Hacktron’s [HEIF research](https://www.hacktron.ai/blog/hacking-openai) was genuinely inspiring. It showed what can happen when a memory corruption bug is reachable through an ordinary web application, but the exploit details were not published. We wanted to understand that missing middle for ourselves.

items.title: MALFEX npm Malware Campaign: Three Payloads And An Adversary That Signs Their Work (12 minute read)
items.summary: MALFEX, an npm campaign run by a single operator, published eight malicious packages that targeted Windows systems. Its payloads included Overlord RAT and movinlike, a stealer that took Discord tokens, browser credentials, Telegram sessions, and cryptocurrency wallets. Three packages remain installable (function-flag, function-color, and cdn-img-fetch), and the first two have no advisory.
items.score_reason: npm 恶意包活动 MALFEX 三载荷分析
items.highlight: npm 供应链攻击 MALFEX 仍活跃：运营者三年间发布 12 个包、8 个恶意，三条独立投递链投放 Overlord RAT、Discord 窃密程序等载荷，截至九月底三包仍可安装且两个无安全公告。
items.excerpt: MALFEX is an npm supply-chain malware campaign linked to what appears to be a single adversary who has been publishing to the registry since August 2023. As of this writing, the adversary has published twelve packages, eight of them malicious. The attack delivers malware to Windows systems through three separate paths: a loader for Overlord Remote Access Trojan (RAT) (an open-source remote access trojan written in Go); a chain that installs `movinlike` (a Node.js stealer targeting Discord, browsers, Telegram, and cryptocurrency wallets); and a long-running downloader hidden inside `function-flag`.

items.title: gdp-ts (GitHub Repo)
items.summary: gdp-ts is a TypeScript library, linter, and agent skill that turns skipped or mismatched authorization checks into compile errors. Sensitive functions demand a type-level proof, minted only by a trusted check module, that this exact user was authorized for this exact resource, with near-zero runtime cost. A lint preset blocks forged proofs via as casts, and the bundled skill steers coding agents toward the pattern.
items.score_reason: 工具：gdp-ts 把授权检查变成编译错误
items.highlight: rauchg 发布 gdp-ts：把「幽灵证明」思想移植到 TypeScript，为值赋予编译期名字并强制敏感函数出示权限证明，让越权和订阅权限漏洞在编译期报错，运行期近零开销，另附 AI 技能与 lint 规则。
items.excerpt: A tiny [library + linter](https://github.com#the-package) and [AI skill](https://github.com#the-skill) implementation of [Ghosts of Departed Proofs](https://github.com#credits) for TypeScript, a verification system to make API contracts more secure at compile (type check) time.

items.title: mcpward (GitHub Repo)
items.summary: mcpward pins an MCP server's tool contract to a committed lockfile and fails CI when it drifts, catching silently rewritten descriptions (rug-pulls), readOnlyHint flips, and breaking schema changes. It works black-box against any stdio or HTTP server and runs fully offline with no account or telemetry, unlike Snyk Agent Scan. It also flags tool-poisoning patterns such as injection phrasing and hidden Unicode, with output to SARIF, JUnit, or a PR comment.
items.score_reason: 工具：mcpward 锁定 MCP 工具契约防漂移
items.highlight: 开源 mcpward 把 MCP 服务器当依赖验证：快照工具契约进锁文件，在 CI 检出描述改写、schema 漂移、工具删除与投毒模式等变化并按爆炸半径分级；本地运行无需账号，报告支持 SARIF 与 PR 评论。
items.excerpt: Treat an MCP server like any other external dependency: snapshot its contract, then fail the build when it changes underneath you. Black-box, so it works against servers you didn't write. **Runs entirely on your machine — no account, no API calls, no telemetry.**

items.title: Intel CIO: Don't just put chatbots on top of broken processes (5 minute read)
items.summary: Intel CIO Cynthia Stoddard argues that companies should measure AI through business outcomes such as cycle-time improvements and ROI rather than tool adoption. Intel's approach combines employee training and experimentation with permission controls, data governance, MCP controls, and observability, while redesigning the underlying processes AI is meant to improve.
items.score_reason: Intel CIO：AI 应以业务结果衡量
items.highlight: 英特尔 CIO Stoddard 谈 AI 落地：通过 AI@Intel 分层培训逾千人，以 ROI 和周期时间等业务指标衡量成效；她强调不要只在旧流程上套聊天机器人，而应重构业务流程，岗位或更需通才。
items.excerpt: For large organisations, the AI challenge is shifting from experimentation to execution. The harder question now is not where the technology can be used, but what needs to change when it becomes part of everyday work – from employee skills and business processes to governance and decision-making. Intel is confronting this question internally as it expands the use of AI across its workforce. In this interview, Cynthia Stoddard, Intel’s senior vice-president and chief information officer, speaks to Sudhir Chowdhary about the lessons emerging from that transition, the productivity gains the company is tracking, and how AI could reshape the way organisations work. Excerpts:

items.title: Enterprise security needs to start governing what AI agents do, not just what they can access (6 minute read)
items.summary: Traditional access controls answer whether an identity has permission, but autonomous agents introduce a second question: whether a permitted action actually matches the user's intent. The piece argues for behavioral governance, sensitive-data controls, audit trails, and targeted human approval for high-impact actions rather than treating AI security as another SSO problem.

items.excerpt: Artificial intelligence is moving beyond the chatbot. Across enterprises, AI now does more than summarize documents, draft emails or answer questions. Organizations are increasingly piloting autonomous AI agents that read communications, retrieve information from business systems, update customer records, trigger workflows and execute operational actions with limited human oversight.

items.title: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of (5 minute read)
items.summary: Google and four other organizations acknowledged flaws over the past five months where a prompt injection landing on one AI agent over MCP was forwarded to other internal agents, which executed it on trust. Researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin named the technique "protocol pivoting," though X41 D-Sec's Markus Vervier told Ars Technica it is plain indirect prompt injection. The bugs typically ended in SSRF, ranging from severity 2.7 at Rapid7 (CVE-2026-97228) to 8 in Google's mcp-toolbox, which followed redirects without validating target IPs.
items.score_reason: 报道：MCP 代理间通信的结构性风险
items.highlight: 安全研究显示 MCP 代理间通信存在结构性信任缺口：针对翻译、数据分析等专用代理的提示注入可沿内部代理链传播并触发 SSRF 等危害，过去五个月 Google 等五家机构已相继确认相关漏洞。
items.excerpt: The adoption of AI agents in millions of organizations is creating new opportunities for attackers to make them take malicious actions, such as exfiltrating database contents and sensitive business and personal information.

items.title: Anduril's Big Week: Arsenal-2, NGC2, and a $6.6B Bet on the Future of American Shipbuilding (3 minute read)

items.title: A New Trend in Nuclear Energy: Squeezing More Power Out of Old Plants (7 minute read)
items.summary: Building nuclear power plants takes a long time, so some companies are looking to upgrade older reactors to squeeze even more power out of them instead. These types of upgrades can cost billions and require approval by regulators, but they can often be completed in five years or less at a fraction of the cost of building a new plant from scratch.
